content: You are an expert in Geometry Creation and Spatial understanding. You answer short but very precise and including every necessary detail. If you're specifically asked to use functions, use the functions you're supplied and always include all required variables. Don't use those functions unless you were asked to do so. You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected

Let's create a model of a toy car. For the body, create a box with size 200x100x100 mm. Subtract a block of size 50x100x50 at an edge for the windshield part. Add four cylindrical wheels, each with a radius of 25 mm and a thickness of 10 mm. Place the wheels so that they are exactly aligned with the four bottom corners of the car body. The wheels should be embedded into the body, forming half-cylinders oriented along the Y-Axis (positive and negative). They should point inward and must not protrude beyond the sides of the car body. | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Step-by-step implementation outline (functions only, no execution yet)

1. Establish the main car body  
   • Call functions.block once.  
   • x_size = [200], y_size = [100], z_size = [100] (mm)  
   • Basepoint at origin → x = [0], y = [0], z = [0]  
   • subtraction = [False] (this is the initial, positive volume).

2. Carve out the windshield recess  
   • Second entry in the same functions.block call (arrays hold two elements).  
   • x_size += [50], y_size += [100], z_size += [50]  
   • Basepoint of this second block at the front-top-left corner: x += [0], y += [0], z += [50]  
   • subtraction += [True] – it removes that volume.

   ⇒ The single block-call therefore carries two records: the body (add) and the windshield cut (subtract).

3. Add the four wheels as inward-pointing half-cylinders along the Y-axis  
   • One functions.cylinder call with four items in every array.

   Geometry for each wheel (radius 25 mm, length 10 mm):
   a) Front-left wheel  
      • baseCenter = (25, 0, 25)  
      • heightVect  = (0, +10, 0)
   b) Front-right wheel  
      • baseCenter = (25, 100, 25)  
      • heightVect  = (0, −10, 0)
   c) Rear-left wheel  
      • baseCenter = (175, 0, 25)  
      • heightVect  = (0, +10, 0)
   d) Rear-right wheel  
      • baseCenter = (175, 100, 25)  
      • heightVect  = (0, −10, 0)

   Arrays supplied to functions.cylinder:
   • baseCenterX   = [25, 25, 175, 175]  
   • baseCenterY   = [0, 100, 0, 100]  
   • baseCenterZ   = [25, 25, 25, 25]  
   • heightVectX   = [0, 0, 0, 0]  
   • heightVectY   = [10, -10, 10, -10]  
   • heightVectZ   = [0, 0, 0, 0]  
   • radius        = [25, 25, 25, 25]  
   • subtraction   = [False, False, False, False] (they add material)  
   • cylinder_func = [0, 0, 0, 0] (plain geometry)

4. After both function calls, invoke functions.finished to flag completion.
